Research Question: Are they more frequent in the summer or winter?


# Introduction

The dataset includes the location data (decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude) along with the months which includes the month when numbats were observed in the corresponding location. With this information, we can understand the frequency of numbats in each season. 

# Analysis

First, I fix the data with the code provided in the class to deal with the NA weather data that we had. Then, I group the months to add a season column that helps creating a dataset with the frequency of observations. Finally, I make a plot of seasonal/monthly variations and map the observations in each season.

```{r}
# I used the code given in the class for this part.

#Numbats
library(tidyverse)

#install.packages("weatherOz")
library(weatherOz)

numbat_data<-read_csv("numbats.csv") %>%
  filter(!is.na(eventDate)) %>%
  mutate(event_day=date(with_tz(eventDate,"Australia/Sydney")),
         event_oz=format(event_day,"%Y%m%d"))

#Only look up weather for records the database can handle
numbat_query<-numbat_data %>%
  filter(event_day>=as.Date("1889-01-01") & is.na(decimalLatitude)==FALSE)

numbat_wx<-function(row_sel){
  numbat_sel<-numbat_query[row_sel,]
  
  get_data_drill(
    longitude=numbat_sel$decimalLongitude,
    latitude=numbat_sel$decimalLatitude,
    start_date=numbat_sel$event_oz,
    end_date=numbat_sel$event_oz,
    values     = c("max_temp", "min_temp", "rain"),
    api_key    = "jshannon@uga.edu"
  ) %>%
    mutate(recordID=numbat_sel$recordID) %>%
    select(-c(longitude,latitude,year,month,day,date))
}

weather_data<-map_df(1:nrow(numbat_query),numbat_wx)

#Join back to the full dataset 
numbat_weather<-numbat_data %>%
  left_join(weather_data,by="recordID")

```
```{r}
# Here, I add a season column and used case_when() to have the seasonal observations.
# Australian seasons are arranged differently so I searched online to get months for each season.

numbat_weather<-numbat_weather %>%
  mutate(season=case_when(
    month %in% c("Dec","Jan","Feb") ~ "Summer",
    month %in% c("Mar","Apr","May") ~ "Autumn",
    month %in% c("Jun","Jul","Aug") ~ "Winter",
    month %in% c("Sep","Oct","Nov") ~ "Spring"),
    season=factor(season,levels=c("Summer","Autumn","Winter","Spring")),
    month=factor(month,levels=month.abb))

# Getting the counts of observations per season
season_count<-numbat_weather %>%
  count(season) %>%
  mutate(pct=n/sum(n)*100)

season_count
```
Numbats are seen most frequently in the Spring followed by Summer, and they are seen least frequent in Winter and Autumn. The difference between these two groups is so large.


```{r}

# Plotting the monthly/seasonal variations.
season_colors<-c("Summer"="darkred","Autumn"="darkorange","Winter"="darkblue","Spring"="darkgreen")

ggplot(numbat_weather,aes(x=month,fill=season))+
  geom_bar()+
  scale_fill_manual("Season",values=season_colors)+
  labs(title="Numbat sightings by month",
       x="Month",y="Number of sightings")+
  theme_minimal()
```
The plot shows that the observations are highest in November and December and lowest in April. Autumn has the lowest observations and Spring has the highest observations.


```{r}


library(sf)
library(tmap)

#Australia shape can be taken from the World dataset that comes with tmap. 
data("World")
australia<-World %>%
  filter(name=="Australia") %>%
  st_transform(4326)

# Spatial dataset to see seasonal locations. 
numbat_season<-numbat_weather %>%
  filter(is.na(decimalLatitude)==FALSE) %>%
  mutate(season=case_when(
    month(event_day) %in% c(12,1,2) ~ "Summer",
    month(event_day) %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Autumn",
    month(event_day) %in% c(6,7,8) ~ "Winter",
    month(event_day) %in% c(9,10,11) ~ "Spring")) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords=c("decimalLongitude","decimalLatitude"),crs=4326,remove=FALSE)


#Summer
map1<-tm_shape(australia)+
  tm_polygons(fill="grey")+
tm_shape(numbat_season %>% filter(season=="Summer"))+
  tm_dots(size=0.2,fill="darkred",fill_alpha=0.5)+
tm_title("Summer")


#Autumn
map2<-tm_shape(australia)+
  tm_polygons(fill="grey")+
tm_shape(numbat_season %>% filter(season=="Autumn"))+
  tm_dots(size=0.2,fill="darkorange",fill_alpha=0.5)+
tm_title("Autumn")


#Winter
map3<-tm_shape(australia)+
  tm_polygons(fill="grey")+
tm_shape(numbat_season %>% filter(season=="Winter"))+
  tm_dots(size=0.2,fill="darkblue",fill_alpha=0.5)+
tm_title("Winter")


#Spring
map4<-tm_shape(australia)+
  tm_polygons(fill="grey")+
tm_shape(numbat_season %>% filter(season=="Spring"))+
  tm_dots(size=0.2,fill="darkgreen",fill_alpha=0.5)+
tm_title("Spring")


tmap_arrange(map1,map2,map3,map4,ncol=2)
```
The spatial variation of observations shows that they mostly appear around the same location in southwest and south-southeast. However, in Spring we can also see some observations in the center. We saw earlier that the frequency was the highest in the Spring, suggesting that Spring has both the highest frequency in both spatial variations and numbers.
